title: Mockito Unit Tests
summary: Control dependency results and assert service behavior without starting Spring.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Mockito Spring Boot Tutorial | @Mock @InjectMocks

richText: A mock supplies controlled dependency behavior
Mockito creates a replacement object for a dependency. The test decides what the mock returns and can check calls made to it. A mock repository does not connect to the database.
Use mocks for boundaries such as repositories or email clients when testing a service’s decisions. Use real value objects and the real service under test.
@Mock creates the mock. @InjectMocks creates the object under test and attempts to inject the mocks. Prefer constructor injection in application code so required dependencies are explicit.
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) initializes Mockito for JUnit Jupiter. This test has no @SpringBootTest, no Spring context and no active application profile.
Test both a result and a boundary call
The compact example defines its dependency and service contract. The service returns a stored title or throws for a missing entry. Mockito controls each repository response.
when(...).thenReturn(...) is stubbing. It prepares the dependency response. verify(...) checks an interaction. assertEquals checks the observable result. These checks answer different questions.
Prefer exact arguments when they are part of the requirement. anyString() can hide a service passing the wrong user ID. Use matchers only when the value is irrelevant to the rule.
If one argument uses a matcher, use matchers for all arguments in that call. eq(value) checks a particular value while other arguments use broader matchers.
Use ArgumentCaptor when the service builds a new object for a dependency. Capture the object and assert meaningful fields such as owner ID or encoded-password status.

For a void dependency, doThrow(...).when(mock).operation(...) simulates failure. Assert the service’s intended failure behavior. Avoid checking every internal call unless order or call count is required.
Keep mock scope distinct from integration scope
@InjectMocks does not apply Spring proxies, transactions, configuration properties or security filters. A Mockito test cannot prove that @Transactional rolls back a database change.
A web slice or full application test needs collaborators registered in the Spring context. Plain @Mock fields do not automatically replace Spring beans.
The tutorial uses manual Mockito initialization in a disabled sample. The Jupiter extension gives each test managed mock setup without loading Spring.
Use a real database integration test for query correctness. Use HTTP tests for request binding and security filters. Keep the Mockito unit test for service decisions and failure paths.
